case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 2nd July. 1996 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision Nos. 10141 and 10189 of 1991).
full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: These two appeals, by leave, are against the judgment of 2nd July, 1996 of a Single Bench of the High Court Division making the Rules absolute obtained in Civil Revision Nos. 10141 and 10189 of 1991 against the judgment and order dated 29th June, 1988 of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet in Miscellaneous appeal No. 95 of 1985 and Miscellaneous Appeal No. 94 of 1985 reversing the judgment and order dated 30th April, 1985 of the Additional Court of Munsif Sadar Sylhet in Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1985 and Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1985 allowing prayer for pre-emption sought under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act 1949 by the respondents (pre-emptors) in the appeals against the respective appellant (pre-emptees) in the respective appeals in respect of the transfer that took place on 27th July, 1978.

2. Pre-emptor's case, in short is that the land sought to be pre-empted and the land they purchased on 25 March, 1974 along with other land belonged to one Ilias Miah son of Meherullah and said Ilias Miah died leaving wife Ful Banu, two sisters Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi and one full brother Younus who died leaving wife Gulesta Banu, two sons and three daughters. The pre-emptors and one Nanu Miah purchased the property from the full sisters of Ilias Miah on 25 March. 1974, that Nanu Miah transferred his share to the pre-emptors on 25 August, 1980, that on 27 July. 1978 Ful Banu wife of Ilias Miah, transferred her share to the pre-emptee in the respective miscellaneous case, that the pre-emptee of the respective Miscellaneous cases are stranger purchasers and that the transfers under pre-emption were made without notice to the pre-emptors.

3. Pre-emptee-appellant in the respective appeals opposed the prayer for pre-emption contending, inter alia that the land sought to be pre-empted originally belonged to Mohiuddin and Ilias Miah came into possession of the land and thereupon land was recorded in his name during the last settlement operation. The pre-emptees denied the claim of the pre-emptors that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah and that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi being not the sisters of Ilias Miah they did not acquire any right, title and interest in the land that belonged to Ilias Miah, that transfer by Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi to the pre-emptors and Nanu Miah was unauthorized since the alleged sisters of Ilias Miah had no right, title and interest in the land of Ilias Miah in any manner. It was the specific case of the pre-emptee of the respective Miscellaneous case that Ilias Miah died issueless leaving his wife Ful Banu and two brothers Rais Miah and Yunus, that there was an amicable partition of the land left by Ilias Miah among his successors and that the land transferred to the pre-emptee of the respective Miscellaneous Cases was allotted to Ful Banu, wife of Ilias Miah and that Ful Banu who was in possession of the land got by amicable partition amongst the successors of Ilias Miah ultimately sold the said land to the pre-emptee of the respective Miscellaneous Cases on 27 July, 1978.

4. The Court of first instance on consideration of the evidence, both oral and documentary, allowed the prayer for preemption in both the Miscellaneous Cases. Thereupon the pre-emptee of the respective Miscellaneous Cases preferred appeals before the Court of District Judge, Sylhet and the said appeals were heard by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, who by the judgment and order dated 29th July, 1998 set aside the judgment and order of the court of first instance and thereupon dismissed the Miscellaneous Cases.

5. As against the judgment of the 2nd Court of Subordinate Judge in the Miscellaneous Appeals, the pre-emptors moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and obtained Rules being Civil Revision No. 10141 of 1991 (against the judgment of Miscellaneous Appeal No. 95 of 1985 which was preferred against the judgment passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 12 of 1985) and Civil Revision No. 10189 of 1991 (against the Judgment of Miscellaneous Appeal No. 94 of 1985 which was preferred against the judgment passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1965 which was preferred against the judgment passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 1985). The High Court Division made the Rule absolute upon observing:

"Though the successors-in-interest of deceased Ilias Miah or not would be sorted out in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 245 of 1979 and Title Suit No. 344 of 1990 but for the purpose of these Miscellaneous Cases. I am of the view that the pre-emptors have, prima facie made out a case that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah or at least that they are the heirs of Ilias Miah in respect of the case land and thereby making them co-sharer tenants in the case land. Accordingly, on the basis of purchase from Kulsuma and Rahima by the pre-emptors, they also became the co-sharer tenants in the case land and as such the applications for pre-emption are maintainable at the instance of the pre-emptors as they had an interest in the case holding as co-sharer tenants."

6. It may be mentioned Title Suit No. 245 of 1979 is for the partition of the properties of lIias Miah and therein Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the proforma defendants. The other title suit, being No. 344 of 1980, is for declaration of title and for a decree of permanent injunction as well as for declaring the decree in SCC Suit Nos. 2 and 3 of 1976 illegal and void.

7. Pre-emptor's claim of pre-emption solely depends on the establishment of the fact that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah. The trial Curt in arriving at the finding that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah placed reliance on the evidence of PW 1, one of the pre-ernptors and PW 2 claimed to be husband of Kulsuma Bibi and the pleadings of the Title Suit No. 245 of 1979 and 344 of 1980. The court of appeal below reversed the finding of the trial Court as regard PW2's claim of being husband of Kulsuma Bibi upon observing that in respect thereof no document, particularly Kabinnama which he admitted was registered and stated that he has the same was not produced, and as such it is not safe to rely on PW2's lone evidence to arrive at a finding that he is the husband of Kulsuma. The court of appeal below further observed that trial court did not discuss the question pertaining to Kulsuma Bibi's and Rahima Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Mian in detail and that did not arrive at a definite finding in that regard. The court of appeal below further observed that merely because Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi have been made parties in the title suit but from that decision cannot be arrived at that they are sisters of Ilias Miah as because, in the respective plaint of the said suits it has been specifically denied that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are not the sisters of Ilias Miah.

8. The High Court Division has reversed the judgment and order of the court of appeal below upon observing that "the pre-emptors have, prima facie made out a case that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah or at least that they are the heirs of Ilias Miah in respect of the case land and thereby making them co-sharer tenants in the case land."

<u>9. PW 1 in his evidence has stated that Ilias Miah died leaving wife Ful Banu, two sisters Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi and brother Yunus. But at the same time PW 1 has stated that he has not filed paper to show that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah and that he came to know from the papers which he had seen at the time of making purchase that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the full sisters of Ilias Miah and they are the daughters of Meherullah. It may be mentioned Ilias Miah is the son of Meherullah. Although PW 1 stated that he came to know from the papers which he saw at the time of making purchase but no such paper was placed before the court in support of his statement of knowing about Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi being the daughters of Meherullah. This witness has further stated that he heard from the relations of Rahim a Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi they are the full sisters of llias Miah but in support of having that information or deriving of the knowledge that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the full sisters of I1ias Miah, no evidence has been led. There is nothing in the evidence of PW 1 that he had any information from PW 2 who claims him to be the husband of Kulsuma Bibi, that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah. So PW 1's evidence as to that Rahima Bibi Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah remains uncorroborated or in other words has not been corroborated by the evidence of any of the witnesses examined by the pre-emptors. Now there remains the evidence of PW 2 who claims himself to be husband of Kulsuma Bibi. This witness has stated that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of I1ias Miah and he is the husband of Kulsuma Bibi. The fact of Rahirna Bibi's and Kulsuma Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah has been denied by the pre-emptees and thereupon it was the duty of the pre-emptors to establish the fact of Kulsuma's and Rahima's being the sisters of Ilias Miah because in the absence of establishing the said fact pre-emptors would not be entitled to have the relief prayed in Miscellaneous Cases. The pre-emptors to prove the fact that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah have examined PW 2. There is no tangible material except the uncorroborated statement of PW 2 that he is the husband of Kulsuma Bibi or in other words PW 2's claim as of being the husband of Kulsuma Bibi has not been corroborated by any other evidence, both oral and documentary. Because of the quality of the evidence of PW 2 it cannot be said that said witness has proved the pre-emptor's claim that Kulsuma and Rahima are the sisters of Ilias Miah. PW 2 claimed that his marriage was registered and that he has the Kabinama. But same has not been produced at any stage of the Miscellaneous Cases. In the background of challenge as to PW 2's being the husband of Kulsuma, said to be the daughter of Meherullah and thereupon full sister of Ilias Miah, the fact of PW 2's being husband of Kulsuma remains legally unestablished. The Kabinnama or any other competent person if would have deposed about the fact of Kulsuma's being wife of PW 2 that could have been the best evidence to resolve the contentious matter' that Kulsuma Bibi is the full sister of Ilias Miah and that PW 2 is the husband of Kulsuma Bibi but that vital material piece of evidence and the evidence of such person has not been brought on record. In the background of the evidence from the side of the pre-emptors as discussed herein above it is seen that the material question i.e. question of Rahima Bibi's and Kulsuma Bibi's being the full' sisters of I1ias Miah has not been resolved by legal evidence and that the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 having not been corroborated by the evidence of independent and reliable witness the same cannot be made the basis for coming to the decision that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah. Evidence of PWs 1 and 2 in no standard can be considered corroborative evidence of each other's evidence as to the material fact Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Miah or that PW 2 is husband of Kulsuma. The High Court Division in our view was in error in reversing the judgment of the court of appeal below upon observing; "pre-emptors have prima facie made a case that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah or at least that they are the heirs of Ilias Miah in respect of the case land and thereby making them co-sharer tenants in the case land" as pre-emptees in case of allowing pre-emption would be deprived of their valuable right to hold property in the absence of firm establishment of the fact that Kulsuma and Rahima are the sisters of Ilias Miah and as such the pre-emptors under the law are required to establish a definite and firm case and not a 'prima facie' case of their being co-sharers of the land sought to be pre-empted. Making out of prima case however strong be, in law cannot be the basis for depriving one of holding property and that to deprive one of one's property there must have case of definite and unassailable kind or quality. In pre- emption proceeding one is deprived of one's property through the coercive' process of the Court and as such unless pre-emptor has a positive case of his being co-sharer the court upon a finding of pre-emptor's having a 'prima facie case' of being co- sharer is not permitted by law to grant pre-emption. Right to acquire and to hold property, subject to restriction imposed by law, is a guaranteed right of a citizen and when a citizen by the coercive process of law is compelled to part with his acquired property, then the condition(s) or the provision of law upon resorting to which a citizen is compelled to part with his property, the same is to be fulfilled in entirety and the provision of law as to coercive parting with properly is to be applied only when there is proof of the fact up to the hilt in the background of which parting with property can be compelled or in other words a citizen would only be compelled to part with his acquired property while the other, who is seeking aid of the court to compel a citizen to part with his property, has established the fact that would have entitled him to have the other's property completely. One cannot compel another upon restoring to a particular provision of law to part with his property in making out a prima facie case for such parting with, as in the instant case of pre-emption. One has to establish one's basis of claim for compelling another to part with his property in one's favour to the full or finally but not upon making out a prima facie case for compelling one to part with one's property by the coercive process of law. In the instant case pre-emptors where required to establish that they are co- sharers of the land transferred to the pre-emptee of the respective Miscellaneous cases and for that pre-emptors were required to establish that Kulsuma and Rahima are the full sisters of Ilias Miah as because in the absence of establishing that Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Miah, since the pre-emptors claim they are co-sharers of the land transferred to pre-emptee of the two miscellaneous cases by purchase from sisters of Ilias Miah, the pre-emptors could not claim pre-emption in .respect of the transfers sought to be pre-empted. The appellate court dismissed the miscellaneous case on the finding that pre-emptors failed- to establish that Kulsuma and Rahima are full sisters of Ilias Mia. The High Court Division allowed the prayer for pre-emption on the finding that pre-emptors made out a prima facie case that Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Miah. The law is now settled that concept of "prima facie case" would only receive consideration of the court while disposing of any interlocutory matter at the primary stage of a case or in other words the case has yet not reached the stage of finality. In the final hearing of the case respective parties thereto would certainly be required to establish or prove their respective case completely or in other words conclusively. There would be total absence of alloy as regards establishment of the case either to have a relief sought from the court or for the rejection of the relief sought by the first party (Plaintiff) in the suit. The High Court Division was in serious error in allowing pre-emption only because prima facie it was established that Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Mia upon overlooking the material fact that establishing something prima facie is never the establishing of the said fact conclusively or finally or that said establishment i.e. prima facie establishment, was free from alloy. Making out of a prima facie case is nothing more than making out a case of first impression or something that appears to be true at the first sight or consideration. A prima facie case is not free from alloy or in other words it cannot be said that prima facie case has stood the acid test. As such establishing or making out of a prima facie case in law cannot be considered to have established the case finally or conclusively or said to have proved the case for having the relief sought by the first party in the proceeding conclusively or in other words free from alloy.</u>

10. The High Court Division also was in error in placing reliance on the plaints of Title Suit No. 245 of 1979 and 344 of 1980 in arriving at the finding as to Kulsuma Bibi's and Rahima Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah in that the plaintiffs of the said suits in the respective plaints have made clear averment denying the fact of Kulsuma Bibi's and Rahima Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah. Merely because Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi have been made proforma-defendants in the aforementioned Title Suits it cannot be said the plaintiffs of the title suits accepted the said two defendants as the sisters of Ilias Miah as because there are statements in the plaints denying their being the sisters of Bias Miah and that there is also explanation in the plaints why these two defendants have been made parties in the suit. The said two title Suits are still pending and in the absence of decision in the said two suits or final disposal of the said two suits it can be said that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah, nor can it be said because of impleading Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi (as defendants) describing them as sisters of Ilias Miah in Tittle Suits a 'prima facie' has been made out by the preemptors as to Kulsuma Bibi's and Rahima Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah. Since the pre-emptors did not establish by legal evidence that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah and that being so it cannot be said in the absence of legally establishing that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah, the pre-emptors by purchase from the said two persons have become co-sharers in the land left by Ilias Miah and that inherited by Ful Banu wife of Ilias Miah and that have acquired right of pre-emption.

In view of the discussion made herein above we find merit in the appeals. Accordingly, the same are allowed. There is no order as to cost.

End.
